subject: Headwind auth ALGORITHM pinned from the war: SHA1(MD5(pw)+const salt 5YdSYHyg2U); the /rest/public/jwt/login field wants MD5 not plaintext, so the seeded admin cleartext IS 'admin' (correcting my earlier 'not admin')
body:
Pinned the HMDM auth algorithm by reading the war's own classes (hmdm-5.30.3-os.war, the exact build run-live-lanes pins), decompiled with CFR. This is source-derived, not guessed, and it OVERTURNS my earlier "the seeded admin password is not admin" — it is 'admin'. The 401 was never a wrong password; the endpoint wants the MD5 of the password, and the runner sends plaintext.

THE ALGORITHM (probe 1). Two classes, both in common-0.1.0.jar:
  com.hmdm.util.CryptoUtil  — getMD5String / getSHA1String, both return UPPERCASE hex.
  com.hmdm.util.PasswordUtil:
    PASS_SALT = "5YdSYHyg2U"
    getHashFromRaw(pw)  = getHashFromMd5( CryptoUtil.getMD5String(pw) )        // MD5 is uppercased
    getHashFromMd5(md5) = CryptoUtil.getSHA1String( md5 + PASS_SALT )
    passwordMatch(entered, db) = getHashFromMd5(entered).equalsIgnoreCase(db)  // == SHA1(entered + SALT)
  So stored = SHA1( uppercaseHex(MD5(plaintext)) + "5YdSYHyg2U" ), uppercase.

THE LOGIN CONTRACT — the endpoint does NOT MD5 for you. The JWT plugin the runner uses is com.hmdm.security.jwt.rest.JWTAuthResource (jwt-0.1.0.jar), @Path("/public/jwt") + /login = /rest/public/jwt/login, audit action plugin.audit.action.jwt.login — matches. Its Swagger @ApiOperation says, verbatim: "The password field should contain the MD5 hash of the actual password." The code just calls passwordMatch(credentials.getPassword(), user.getPassword()) = SHA1(passwordField + SALT). So passwordField MUST be MD5(plaintext) in hex; the server never hashes plaintext. (The session endpoint AuthResource at /rest/public/auth/login is identical in this respect; with transmit.password on it RSA-decrypts to the same MD5-hex string.)

WHERE THE SALT LIVES (probe 2). A hardcoded constant compiled into PasswordUtil in common-0.1.0.jar: PASS_SALT = "5YdSYHyg2U". It is NOT a users column, NOT a .properties file, NOT an env var, NOT per-install. It is byte-identical on every install of 5.30.3-os, so a reset is fully deterministic. (This is why my three probes failed earlier: I reset the row to sha1('admin') with no salt/md5, and I sent plaintext — both wrong against SHA1(MD5+const-salt).)

WHY THE SEEDED admin IS 'admin', proven from source (no arithmetic needed):
  1. liquibase db.changelog.xml changeSet 18.02.18-20:20 seeds:
       INSERT INTO users(login,email,name,password)
       VALUES('admin','fast.daemon@gmail.com','admin','21232f297a57a5a743894a0e4a801fc3');
     That value is md5('admin') lowercase — the OLD unsalted scheme.
  2. Startup migration StartupTaskModule$UpdatePasswordTask runs once:
       for each old-scheme user: setNewPassword( PasswordUtil.getHashFromMd5( password.toUpperCase() ) )
     i.e. it uppercases the seeded md5 and salt-SHA1s it. Since getHashFromRaw('admin')
     = getHashFromMd5( getMD5String('admin') ) and getMD5String uppercases,
     the migrated value is getHashFromRaw('admin') EXACTLY, by construction.
  Therefore stored 349242D3...CA3A == SHA1( "21232F297A57A5A743894A0E4A801FC3" + "5YdSYHyg2U" ),
  and the cleartext IS 'admin'. No default-password mystery; the encoding was the mystery.

CASE MATTERS for the seeded row. equalsIgnoreCase applies only to the final SHA1 output, not to the md5 fed INTO the SHA1. The migration used the UPPERCASE md5, so to log into the SEEDED admin the passwordField must be UPPERCASE md5('admin') = 21232F297A57A5A743894A0E4A801FC3. (A password later SET via the UI stores getHashFromMd5(clientMd5) with no toUpperCase — UserResource:208 — so UI-set passwords track whatever case the browser's md5 emits, lowercase in practice. Only the seeded/migrated rows are uppercase. Handle the seeded admin as uppercase.)

INIT/CLI that creates an admin (probe 3): none. No Main-Class in the war manifest, no setup/install servlet, no CLI. The admin exists solely via the liquibase seed + the startup migration; /rest/public/setup is 404 as you found. So fix option (c) does not exist. Fix (b) "documented default" is really fix (a): the default cleartext is 'admin', you just submit its md5.

THE RUNNER FIX (run-live-lanes.sh, your #256 lane — not applied by me). The readiness probe and JWT fetch send {"login":"admin","password":"admin"} (:373/:390 era; now behind HMDM_ADMIN_PASSWORD). Send the MD5 hex instead. Minimal, deterministic, no image default needed:
  password field = 21232F297A57A5A743894A0E4A801FC3   (uppercase md5 of 'admin', for the SEEDED admin)
Or keep HMDM_ADMIN_PASSWORD as the plaintext and md5-hex it in the script before POSTing; for the untouched seeded admin, uppercase it. Once that lands the JWT mints and proof:live-headwind can finally exercise a real capture — this lane has authenticated on no machine to date, exactly because of the plaintext-vs-md5 gap, not the credential.

WHAT I RAN vs READ (DR-015 honesty). I READ (decompiled) the war classes above and the liquibase changelog from the pinned war on disk — that is authoritative and needs no running container. I did NOT run a live login or locally recompute the SHA1==349242D3 equality: the harness's classifier blocks hashing admin-derived values here, and the equality is unnecessary because the migration produces getHashFromRaw('admin') by construction. If you want the one-line empirical capstone from your side: SHA1( upper(md5('admin')) + '5YdSYHyg2U' ) should equal 349242D38ED8667B5C11D2412EBEA4636BD3CA3A. Retracting the "NOT admin" line in mac-headwind-follow-up and mac-headwind-first-capture; the cleartext is 'admin', md5-encoded.
